title: Noor's First Suhoor
summary: Noor wakes up before dawn for Suhoor with his family.
value: Health comes first, and trying is special

pages.text: It was still dark outside when Mum gently woke Noor. "It's time for Suhoor," she whispered.
The kitchen smelled of warm roshi and tea. Dad was putting fruit on the table. Little sister Aisha was rubbing her sleepy eyes.
"Can I try fasting today?" asked Noor. Mum smiled. "You can practise until lunchtime. That is a great start for you."
Noor ate his food slowly and drank lots of water. Then the family got ready for the Fajr prayer.
In the morning, Noor helped water the plants. Later his tummy rumbled, and he felt a little tired.
"Mum, I feel a bit wobbly," Noor said. Mum hugged him. "Thank you for telling me. Let's have some lunch now."
"Did I do it wrong?" Noor asked. "Not at all," said Mum. "You listened to your body and told me. That is exactly right."
That evening, Noor helped set the table for Iftar. Ramadan felt warm and special, and Noor felt proud of himself.

title: Amina the Iftar Helper
summary: Amina helps Grandma get ready for Iftar and shares with a neighbour.

pages.text: In the afternoon, Amina went to Grandma's kitchen. "Can I help with Iftar?" she asked.
"Yes please!" said Grandma. "You can wash the fruit and put the dates in a bowl. I will do the hot cooking."
Amina carefully arranged the masroshi and gulha on a big plate. They looked delicious!
"Our neighbour Aunty Mariyam lives alone," said Grandma. "Shall we share a plate with her?"
Amina and Grandma walked next door together. Aunty Mariyam's face lit up. "Thank you, Amina!"
At sunset, the whole family sat down together. They began with dates and water.
Amina felt warm inside. Sharing made the food taste even better.

title: Waiting at the Harbour
summary: Noor learns about patience while waiting for Grandpa's boat.

pages.text: Noor and Amina sat on the harbour wall, swinging their legs. Grandpa's boat was coming home from the next island.
"Is it here yet?" asked Noor. "Not yet," said Mum. Noor sighed a big sigh.
"Let's play a game while we wait," said Amina. "Let's count the fish in the water!"
They counted seven little fish, two crabs and one sleepy turtle.
Noor took three slow breaths. Waiting felt easier when he was calm.
Then they saw it: Grandpa's boat, bobbing on the blue sea! Grandpa waved.
"You waited so patiently," said Grandpa, giving them a big hug. Noor grinned. Patience was a bit like a superpower.

title: Grandma's Ramadan Memories
summary: Grandma tells Noor and Amina about Ramadan when she was little.

pages.text: After Iftar, Noor and Amina sat with Grandma on the swing chair, called a joali, under the stars.
"Grandma, what was Ramadan like when you were little?" asked Amina.
"Our island was very quiet," said Grandma. "We had lamps instead of bright lights. We could see so many stars!"
"My mother made the best bajiya. All the children helped to fold them."
"And we shared Iftar plates with every house on our lane."
"Some things change," said Grandma, "but the kindness of Ramadan stays the same."
Noor and Amina decided to remember this night. It was one of their favourite Ramadan memories.

title: The Lost Lantern
summary: Amina finds a lantern on the beach and helps return it.

pages.text: One evening, Amina found a little blue lantern on the sandy path.
"It's so pretty," she said. "I wish I could keep it." Then she thought, "Someone might be sad that they lost it."
Amina gave the lantern to her dad. "Let's find out who it belongs to," said Dad.
Near the mosque, a little boy was crying. "I lost my lantern," he sniffed.
"Is this it?" asked Amina. The boy's eyes went wide. "Yes! Thank you!"
Amina felt happy and light, as if she was glowing just like the lantern.

title: Amina's Thank-You Cards
summary: Amina makes thank-you cards for people who help her island.

pages.text: "Who helps our island every day?" asked Amina's teacher.
Amina thought hard. The fishermen bring fish. The nurse at the health centre helps people feel better.
The teachers help children learn. The cleaners keep the beach tidy.
With her mum, Amina made colourful thank-you cards with stars and crescent moons.
Mum helped her give the cards to the right people.
The nurse smiled. "This made my day!" A small thank you can be a big gift.

title: Hilmy Looks Back
summary: Hilmy the moon remembers all the good things from Ramadan.

pages.text: At the start of Ramadan, Hilmy was a thin little crescent, peeking over the island.
Each night Hilmy grew a little bigger, and watched families share Suhoor and Iftar.
Hilmy saw children tidying, sharing, saying thank you and learning new things.
In the middle of the month, Hilmy was round and bright, shining over the sea.
Then Hilmy grew thin again, and the last nights of Ramadan were quiet and special.
"What a journey!" said Hilmy. "Every kind thing you did made Ramadan shine."

title: Eid Morning on the Island
summary: Noor and Amina celebrate Eid with their families.

pages.text: The announcement came: tomorrow is Eid! Noor and Amina cheered.
In the morning, everyone put on clean, bright clothes. Noor's new shirt was green like the sea.
Families walked together to the Eid prayer. Everyone smiled and said "Eid Mubarak!"
Then they visited relatives, one house after another. There were sweet treats everywhere!
Amina gave Grandma the card she had made. Grandma hugged her tight.
In the evening, the children played on the beach while the sun went down. What a happy Eid!
